q: Is the {{SITE_NAME}} business name generator free?
a: Yes. It is completely free, there is no sign-up and there is no limit on how many names you can generate. The site is supported by advertising.

q: Are the generated names available to register?
a: Not necessarily. The names are created automatically in your browser, and we do not check them against company registers, trademark databases or domain registries. Use the "Check domain" links on each result, then search the CRO (Ireland) or Companies House (UK) and the trademark registers before you use a name.

q: Can I use a name from the generator for my business?
a: You are free to use any idea you find here, and we do not claim any rights over the suggestions. It is your responsibility to make sure the name does not infringe someone else's trademark or existing business name.

q: Do I need to register my business name in Ireland?
a: If you trade under any name other than your own true name (or, for a company, its registered company name), you must register it as a business name with the Companies Registration Office within one month of starting to use it. The online fee is currently €20 via CORE. Registering a business name does not give you exclusive rights to it; a trademark does that.

q: Should I get a .ie or a .com domain?
a: If most of your customers are in Ireland, a .ie domain signals that you are local and is well trusted. You need a provable connection to the island of Ireland to register one. If you sell internationally, a .com is the safer default. Many businesses buy both and point one at the other. See our domain name guide.

q: What makes a good business name?
a: A good name is easy to say and spell, hints at what you do or how you want customers to feel, is not already used by a competitor, and has a domain and social handle you can get. Short and distinctive usually beats long and clever.
